sources.title: Handley Page Halifax LK794 (WMR 12805)
sources.summary: Our capture of the IWM record. Gives the plaque inscription (578 Squadron, Burn to Caen, LK-Q fire, Canadian rear gunner baled out, six lost and commemorated at Runnymede), six names, location at Carpenters Wood off Dungrove Hill Lane, and two photos by Paul Clarke. Web search summaries of the live page add that the plaque was unveiled on 18 July 1998 and that the 578 Burn Association is responsible; the capture's History/Commemoration sections were empty.
key_details: Carpenters Wood, Dungrove Hill Lane, Burchetts Green

sources.title: Lest We Forget: Flying Officer Victor Starkoff DFC
sources.summary: Reproduces Australian War Memorial roll-of-honour style text for Starkoff and lists the whole seven-man crew with ranks, service numbers, air forces, roles and fate. Names the aircraft as Halifax LK974, takeoff from Burn 0520 for Caen, starboard engine fire at 8,000 ft and a crash at Bisham, Berkshire. The text appears to derive from the AWM (service number page awm.gov.au/collection/P10317700), so it may not be independent of the AWM.

paragraphs.text: On the morning of 18 July 1944, 21 Halifax III bombers of 578 Squadron took off from Burn in North Yorkshire to attack fortified villages near Caen. One of them, coded LK-Q, caught fire on the outward flight and the crew could not put it out. The plaque says the pilot steered clear of Reading and Maidenhead before the aircraft exploded and fell into the wood where the memorial now stands.

Six of the seven crew died. The Canadian rear gunner baled out and survived; the plaque says the others were lost without trace and are named on the Runnymede Memorial. The six names on the stone are the pilot, Flying Officer Victor Starkoff DFC of the RAAF, aged 33; navigator Pilot Officer Jan Fink, 26; wireless operator Pilot Officer Lloyde Hopper of the RCAF; air bomber Flight Sergeant Ivor Morgan, 20; flight engineer Sergeant Gerald Nicholson, 20, from Liverpool; and mid-upper gunner Flight Sergeant John Claque. An Australian museum page, which appears to copy the Australian War Memorial, names the surviving rear gunner as Flight Sergeant H C Sloan, RCAF.

Sources disagree on the serial. The IWM register and the IBCC losses database give LK794; the Australian museum page and Traces of War give LK974. Our record's LK794 follows the two institutional sources. The same museum page puts the crash at Bisham, while IWM places the memorial at Carpenters Wood, Burchetts Green; the two places are near each other.
IWM records the plaque as brushed stainless steel on an oak stand, unveiled on 18 July 1998, with the 578 Burn Association responsible for it.

notes: SERIAL: our record (LK794) is supported by IWM and IBCC (via search summaries). The AWM-derived Aviation Museum of WA page and TracesOfWar say LK974; AWM wording looks like a transposition but unconfirmed. LK794 also appears on backtonormandy.org as LK-Q on a 17 July 1944 Caen sortie flown by F/Sgt H C Sloan, which fits the same aircraft the day before. The earlier doubt (nothing tying LK794 to Burchetts Green) is resolved: the IWM text, six names and the 578 Sqn crew list all match one loss. DATE and TYPE are right. The Aviation Museum page says the crash was at Bisham, which neighbours Burchetts Green. The Aviation Museum page gives takeoff from Burn at 0520. LIMITS: IBCC direct page fetches returned HTTP 429, so IBCC details (ages 33/26/20, LK794) come from search-result summaries, not full page reads; re-check on IBCC. No IBCC entry found for Claque or Hopper (search found nothing; may be spelling, e.g. Claque vs Clague). Hopper is first-named Lloyd in Canadian sources, Lloyde on the stone. Service numbers rest on one source (the AWM-derived museum page); CWGC pages were not reached (CWGC casualty search found no matching record), so no CWGC URLs are given. Ages for Hopper, Claque not found. Nicholson's NatWest page is a staff memorial, not independent of family-supplied data. Starkoff AWM page: https://www.awm.gov.au/collection/P10317700 (not fetched). Dedication date and 578 Burn Association responsibility come from search summaries of the live IWM page; the capture lacks them. No sign of a local parish or landowner custodian beyond the Association; no 578 Burn Association website found. Not followed: 578 Squadron Association site, Berkshire crash-site researchers, the Reading/Maidenhead local press, National Archives AIR 27 ORB, CWGC pages.
